task.instructions: Experiment E3 (tests H13): Cluster-per-image kernel for the 7x7 and 14x14 rows (hidden slices in smem, DSMEM reductions, no grid barrier), with cluster-occupancy, DSMEM and TFLOAT32-rounding probes; other shapes dispatched to the anchor path. Step 0 probes (<= 20 min, record each as a finding): (a) cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters for cluster sizes 8 and 16 (cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed) with 200 KB dynamic smem and 256 threads per CTA: how many clusters run concurrently and the launch-to-first-instruction latency under harness timing; (b) DSMEM microbench in clocks: 16 CTAs all-gather a 75 KB fp16 tile (each writes its 1/16 into every CTA via st.shared::cluster) and reduce-scatter 16 x [768 x 49] fp32 partials (each CTA reads 15 slices via ld.shared::cluster); (c) H14: TMA-load fp32 values with chosen low mantissa bits through a TFLOAT32 tensor map and check bit-exactly whether the result is round-to-nearest or truncation. If (a) gives fewer than 6 concurrent 16-CTA clusters, use 8-CTA clusters (two clusters per image pair is not allowed; use 8 slices of 4C/8). Step 1 kernel, for 2/8/16/32,768,7,7 and 8/16,384,14,14 (dispatch every other shape to the anchor's cooperative kernel copied from the r0 baseline): one cluster per image (two 7x7 images per cluster when B >= 8), CTA j owns C/G channels for the dwconv (zero-padded smem planes) and hidden slice j of 4C/G. LN: per-token partial sums exchanged through DSMEM (one cluster barrier), each CTA normalises its channels and writes the fp16 a tile [tokens][C] into every CTA's smem via st.shared::cluster (second barrier). GEMM1 swap-AB: A = W1 slice [4C/G x C] (fp32 from global/L2 converted to fp16 in smem, or TF32 if (c) confirms rounding), B = a^T, N = tokens; use whichever engine you can get correct in the session (mma.sync FP16 is acceptable; tcgen05 is not required for the thesis). GELU (exact erf) in registers; gf_k = sqrt(sum over tokens of h^2) is thread-local per hidden channel; one DSMEM reduce of the per-CTA partial sums of gf gives mean_k gf (third barrier); s_k = 1 + gw_k*gf_k/(mean+eps), h' = s_k*h + gb_k in registers, written fp16 to the CTA's own smem. GEMM2 partial: W2[:, slice] [C x 4C/G] x h'^T -> [C x tokens] fp32; reduce across the cluster by DSMEM reduce-scatter (CTA j finalises output channels j*C/G .. (j+1)*C/G: + b2 + x, store NCHW with lanes along hw). Weights: each CTA reads only its two slices (1.2 MB at C=768) and ideally once per cluster via TMA multicast or plain L2 reads; measure which. Time each phase in clocks for one cluster at 32,768,7,7 and compare with the 12 us kill criterion from the probe. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times. Success: 16/16 pass; rented <= 30 us at 2,768,7,7 and 8,768,7,7, <= 45 us at 16,768,7,7 and 32,768,7,7, <= 40 us at 8/16,384,14,14 (anchor: 124-1217 us); projected portal score >= 0.50 with the other 10 rows still on the anchor path; probe numbers (concurrent clusters, DSMEM gather/reduce clocks, TFLOAT32 rounding) recorded. Refuted if: fewer than 4 concurrent 8-CTA clusters, or weight-slice ingest plus one GEMM1 per CTA > 12 us at 32,768,7,7 under harness timing, or DSMEM all-gather of the 75 KB a tile > 3 us; any of these means the cluster path cannot beat ~30 us per row and the lineage is retired after incubation with the probe numbers as its conclusions. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).
